1718.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1718.tx: Baaj: band baaj; 'do ungli ka baaj' or 'chanti ka baaj', played mainly with the index and middle fingers; Ta/Dha struck sharply on the chanti; the bayan played without lifting the hand, with little meend.

1719.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1719.tx: Compositions: peshkar, kayda and rela dominate; even the peshkar is expanded like a kayda, in the order of the mukh's bols. It is the most restrictive gharana. Kaydas are mostly chatusra jati; the kayda is presented as mukh, dohra, bal, palta, tihai; solos …

1720.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1720.tx: Bols: dhite, tite, kite, dhage, dhagena, dhinagena, two-finger DRDR. Artists: Ut. Gamme Khan (brought taals other than Teentaal into Delhi), Ut. Inam Ali Khan (last major khalifa), Ut. Natthu Khan (famous for fast two-finger DRDR kaydas). Gharana 2: Lucknow

1721.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1721.tx: Founder and origin: Ut. Modu Khan and Ut. Bakshu Khan, students of the Delhi gharana, within about 50 years of Delhi. The Nawabs of Lucknow supported Kathak, and Kathak's tatkar sounded better with tabla than with pakhawaj; so they built a new style from Ka…

1722.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1722.tx: Baaj: khula baaj, also called hatheli ka baaj, thapiya ka baaj or poorab baaj; the lav instead of the chanti on the tabla, the maidan on the bayan, and a thaap made by closing four fingers.

1723.ti: Gharana: origin and necessity; two gharanas in detail
1723.tx: Compositions: gat, gat-paran, tukda and chakradhar dominate; kaydas are few and carry the language of gat (e.g. 'ghidan'). 'Tukda' comes from 'paran ka tukda'. Pre-composed bandishes are important, and a solo may start without a peshkar.

1789.tx: Birth and family: born 1867 in Mehmood Ganj, Lucknow; son of Ut. Mohammad Khan, a renowned musician and associate of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. Training: learnt from his father from the age of 7, and also from his elder brother Ut. Bade Munne Khan.

1790.tx: Career: taught tabla at Marris Music College, Lucknow (now Bhatkhande Hindustani Sangeet Mahavidyalaya); for a long time accompanied the famous Kathak dancer Pt. Thakur Prasad; khalifa of the Lucknow gharana.

1791.tx: Style: powerful and sparkling (tejasvi) presentation in the khula baaj of Lucknow, suited to Kathak accompaniment. Students: his son-in-law Ut. Wajid Hussain, Pt. Biru Mishra of Banaras, Shri Hirendra Kumar Ganguli of Kolkata, Jahangir Khan; he also taught …

1934.tx: Structure: a rectangular wooden box with keys; one octave has 12 keys (7 white, 5 black); bellows at the back (hand-pumped in India). Playing: the player pumps air with one hand through a flap; pressing a key lets the compressed air vibrate the reed.

1937.ti: Instruments used in Indian music (any three)
1937.tx: Type and origin: avanaddha; a modern form of the ancient pushkar, also called muraj; possibly the 'father' of the tabla; became popular in its present form around the 14th century / Mughal period.

1938.ti: Instruments used in Indian music (any three)
1938.tx: Structure: a horizontal wooden barrel with hide on both faces; the right face has syahi, the left face gets a wheat-flour paste for a deep bass. Playing: palms and fingers; powerful, open, resonant bols (dhumkit, gadigan, dhet, parans).

1969.tx: Structure of the taal: Bhatkhande clearly shows sam, every taali, khaali and every vibhag. Paluskar shows sam, taali and khaali but not the vibhag, because the line comes only at the end.

1970.tx: Position of the taali: in Bhatkhande we read the taali's serial number, so we must count to find which matra it falls on. In Paluskar the matra number itself is written, so the position is read directly.

1971.tx: Value of each bol: Bhatkhande puts one arc under any matra with many bols, so we cannot tell how the matra was divided; for example a tisra 1/6 and a chatusra 1/8 look the same. Paluskar gives each bol its own duration sign, so the jati of every matra is cl…

1972.tx: Limits: Paluskar has no sign for 1/5 or 1/7 of a matra, so Kuaad and Biaad cannot be shown properly in it. Bhatkhande can express every jati, which is why papers ask for Kuaad/Biaad in Bhatkhande notation.

1973.tx: Speed of writing: Bhatkhande is quicker and simpler, so it is preferred for long compositions. Paluskar takes more time but is better for showing jati and small layakaris such as tigun and chaugun. Use today: Bhatkhande notation is more widely used in North…

1974.tx: Conclusion: Both systems have advantages and limits. Bhatkhande is fast and shows the taal's structure (vibhag, taali, khaali) clearly; Paluskar is slower but shows the exact value and jati of each bol. A good student should be able to write in both. Part B…

2022.tx: Riyaz is regular, disciplined practice. The tabla is a pair: the dayan (right hand) gives clear bol-nikas, tite/tirakita, layakari and speed; the bayan (left hand) gives meend, ghumak and an open, resonant naad. Ideal riyaz trains both hands equally, so tha…

2023.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2023.tx: Ideal practice methods Fixed time every day: practise at a set time daily; regularity makes the hand 'riyazi'. Slow to fast: start in thah and move thah → dugun → tigun → chaugun, keeping every bol clear and the wrist relaxed; speed must never break the bols.

2024.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2024.tx: Both hands equally (dayan-bayan balance): practise the same bol or kayda with both hands together, so that every Dha sounds the same.

2025.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2025.tx: Correct nikas, right hand: Dha/Ta with the index finger straight on the chanti, vertical movement of about 1–1½ inches; tite with two fingers in the middle of the syahi (practice phrase 'dhatidhati… dhitedhite'); tirakita with all four letters evenly spaced…

2026.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2026.tx: Correct nikas, left hand: keep the whole hand on the bayan (not just the wrist); ghe-ghe with a vertical pull and release; practise meend and the open naad after Dha/Dhin. Naad awareness: know soft and hard sounds; playing loudly is not the goal; strength a…

2027.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2027.tx: Tuning: keep the dayan tuned to the lehra's Sa; practising on an out-of-tune tabla spoils the ear. Padhant with riyaz: recite the bols while showing taali-khaali; it fixes the composition in memory, teaches the weight of bols and builds confidence.

2031.ti: Ideal practice methods (riyaz) for tabla / pakhawaj
2031.tx: Conclusion: Ideal riyaz is regular, at a fixed time, slow to fast, with both hands balanced, correct nikas, awareness of naad, a tuned instrument and padhant. Strength and nazakat both come only from such daily discipline.

2091.tx: A gharana is a musical tradition or lineage: a particular style of playing passed down from guru to shishya, or within a family, generation after generation, with its own technique (nikas), bol-language, repertoire of compositions and way of thinking. In ea…

2092.tx: How a gharana is formed (origination) Among many students who play exactly like the guru, one student thinks differently, learns from other styles and creates a new style.

2093.tx: If the new style is followed for at least three generations, it is accepted as a gharana. It is usually named after the founder's town (Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farrukhabad, Banaras, Punjab).

2094.tx: Tabla gharanas began around the 18th century; at Emperor Muhammad Shah's court khayal grew popular and tabla began to accompany it. Royal patronage let musicians practise without worry; rivalry between gharanas also pushed students to practise harder; secre…

2095.tx: Necessity of gharanas Preservation: in the oral guru-shishya tradition, the gharana kept compositions, technique and knowledge alive across generations. Discipline and depth: long, systematic training in one style gave depth, purity of nikas and command ove…

2096.tx: Identity and variety: each gharana gave tabla a different colour (closed vs open baaj, kayda vs gat), which enriched the instrument as a whole. Thought system: more than the baaj, a gharana is a way of thinking: how to compose, expand and present. Delhi and…

2097.tx: Today: artists learn from several gurus and mix compositions; many senior players say only one baaj remains. Still, knowing gharanas helps a player understand the origin and correct nikas of each composition. Gharana · Founder · Baaj · Delhi · Ut. Siddhar K…

2101.tx: Baaj: band baaj; 'do ungli ka baaj' or 'chanti ka baaj', played mainly with the index and middle fingers; Ta/Dha struck sharply on the chanti; the bayan played without lifting the hand, with little meend.

2102.tx: Compositions: peshkar, kayda and rela dominate; even the peshkar is expanded like a kayda, in the order of the mukh's bols. It is the most restrictive gharana. Kaydas are mostly chatusra jati; the kayda is presented as mukh, dohra, bal, palta, tihai; solos …

2103.tx: Bols: dhite, tite, kite, dhage, dhagena, dhinagena, two-finger DRDR. Artists: Ut. Gamme Khan (brought taals other than Teentaal into Delhi), Ut. Inam Ali Khan (last major khalifa), Ut. Natthu Khan (famous for fast two-finger DRDR kaydas). Gharana 2: Lucknow

2104.tx: Founder and origin: Ut. Modu Khan and Ut. Bakshu Khan, students of the Delhi gharana, within about 50 years of Delhi. The Nawabs of Lucknow supported Kathak, and Kathak's tatkar sounded better with tabla than with pakhawaj; so they built a new style from Ka…

2105.tx: Baaj: khula baaj, also called hatheli ka baaj, thapiya ka baaj or poorab baaj; the lav instead of the chanti on the tabla, the maidan on the bayan, and a thaap made by closing four fingers.

2106.tx: Compositions: gat, gat-paran, tukda and chakradhar dominate; kaydas are few and carry the language of gat (e.g. 'ghidan'). 'Tukda' comes from 'paran ka tukda'. Pre-composed bandishes are important, and a solo may start without a peshkar.

2107.tx: Artists: Ut. Abid Hussain (taught at Marris College, Lucknow), Ut. Wajid Hussain (khalifa; rela, gat, gat-paran), Ut. Afaq Hussain; today Pt. Swapan Chaudhuri. Point · Delhi · Lucknow · Baaj · Band; chanti ka baaj · Khula; hatheli / poorab baaj ·

2124.tx: रचनाएँ: गत, गत-परन, तुकड़ा और चक्रधार प्रधान; कायदे कम, और उनमें भी गत की भाषा (जैसे 'घिडान')। 'तुकड़ा' शब्द 'परन का तुकड़ा' से आया। पूर्व-रचित बंदिशें अहम, और एकल कभी पेशकार के बिना भी शुरू होता है।

2127.ti: किन्हीं दो घरानों की वादन विशेषताएँ
2127.tx: निष्कर्ष: घराना एक जीवित विचार-परंपरा है। दिल्ली ने तबले को पेशकार, कायदा और रेले की अपनी भाषा दी; लखनऊ ने उसे नृत्य और पखावज की रचनाओं के लिए खोला। घरानों का ज्ञान बताता है कि हर रचना कहाँ से आई और उसे कैसे बजना चाहिए।

2131.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples

2132.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2132.tx: First the total number of matras is fixed. In accompaniment this depends on the main artist's composition: dhrupad-dhamar use taals with many matras; khayal taals are shorter (at most 16 matras), though some have 7 or 12.

2133.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2133.tx: Rasa and length: shringar rasa (love, beauty, a light mood) suits short taals, e.g. Dadra (6), Rupak (7), Keherwa (8) in ghazals. Shanta and gambhir rasa need detailed expression and time, so long taals, often in vilambit or madhya laya, suit them. Principl…

2134.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2134.tx: The matras are divided into vibhags. The pattern decides the taal's character: all equal (samapadi, e.g. Teentaal 4-4-4-4), repeating pairs (ardhasamapadi, e.g. Jhaptaal 2-3-2-3), or all unequal (vishampadi, e.g. Dhamar 5-2-3-4).

2135.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2135.tx: A new taal should try a vibhag pattern different from an existing taal with the same matras; otherwise it will only be another theka of the old taal, not a new taal. (Sooltaal and Jhaptaal both have 10 matras but different vibhags.)

2136.tx: Each vibhag should have a minimum and maximum number of matras. ⚑ Your notes say 2 to 5 (Rules for Designing New Taals); a past ABGMVM true/false and VP-14 say 3 to 5. Note that standard taals such as Ektaal, Jhaptaal and Rupak have 2-matra vibhags, which s…

2137.tx: Principle 3: Place taali and khaali Taali (sashabd kriya) marks heavy (bhari) vibhags; khaali (nishabd kriya) marks the empty vibhag. Sam is the first matra and the strongest point. Khaali is placed so that there is a meaningful contrast between bhari and k…

2138.tx: Khaali never comes twice in a row. Principle 4: Fill in the bols (theka) Bols are filled in so that they express the taal's character; the theka is the 'first bandish' of the taal and must strictly follow its vibhag and taali-khaali, so that a listener can …

2139.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2139.tx: Bols like 'din' and 'titekatagadigana' suggest khula baaj (taals inspired by pakhawaj); such taals do not sound good in bandh baaj. Other thekas may be played in either baaj as needed.

2140.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2140.tx: The mood (classical, semi-classical, light) decides the choice of bols and nikas; a taal can have several thekas (e.g. Tilwada is a theka of 16 matras with Teentaal's vibhags), but no theka may break the taal's boundaries. Principle 5: Basis in the dash pra…

2141.ti: Laws (rules) of taal creation, with examples
2141.tx: The ten pranas (kaal, marg, kriya, ang, graha, jati, kala, laya, yati, prastar) are the theoretical basis of a taal. In ancient music every new taal had to follow all ten; in modern Hindustani music graha, jati, laya, yati and prastar matter most. A taal mu…

2146.tx: ''ताल निर्माण के नियम'' – सोदाहरण जानकारी लिखे।

2148.tx: ताल संगीत में समय नापने की व्यवस्था है। यह तय मात्राओं वाला एक 'खाली कैनवास' है, जिसके अंदर सब रचनाएँ रखी जाती हैं। पुराने ग्रंथ इसे नापने का साधन कहते हैं: संगीत मकरंद के अनुसार समय का व्यावहारिक और चक्र के रूप में बँटवारा; संगीत रत्नाकर के अनुसार वह माध्य…

2149.tx: सिद्धांत 1: मात्राओं की संख्या तय करना सबसे पहले कुल मात्राएँ तय होती हैं। संगत में यह मुख्य कलाकार की रचना पर निर्भर है: ध्रुपद-धमार में ज़्यादा मात्रा वाले ताल; ख़याल के ताल छोटे (ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा 16 मात्रा), कुछ 7 या 12 के भी।

2150.tx: रस और लंबाई: शृंगार रस (प्रेम, सौंदर्य, हल्का भाव) के लिए छोटे ताल ठीक हैं, जैसे ग़ज़ल में दादरा (6), रूपक (7), कहरवा (8)। शांत और गंभीर रस में भाव विस्तार से कहने होते हैं और समय चाहिए, इसलिए लंबे ताल, अक्सर विलंबित या मध्य लय में। सिद्धांत 2: खंड / विभाग …

2151.tx: मात्राओं को विभागों में बाँटा जाता है। विभाग की बनावट से ताल का स्वभाव बनता है: सब बराबर (समपदी, जैसे तीनताल 4-4-4-4), जोड़ी में दोहराते (अर्धसमपदी, जैसे झपताल 2-3-2-3), या सब असमान (विषमपदी, जैसे धमार 5-2-3-4)।

2152.tx: नई ताल में उतनी ही मात्रा वाले पुराने ताल से अलग विभाग-बनावट रखें; नहीं तो वह नई ताल नहीं, पुराने ताल का दूसरा ठेका भर लगेगी। (सूलताल और झपताल दोनों 10 मात्रा के हैं, पर विभाग अलग हैं।)

2153.tx: हर विभाग में कम से कम और ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा मात्राएँ तय हों। ⚑ आपके नोट्स (Rules for Designing New Taals) 2 से 5 कहते हैं; ABGMVM के एक पुराने सही/गलत प्रश्न और VP-14 के अनुसार 3 से 5। ध्यान दें, एकताल, झपताल और रूपक जैसे प्रचलित तालों में 2 मात्रा के विभाग…

2154.tx: सिद्धांत 3: ताली और खाली रखना ताली (सशब्द क्रिया) भारी विभाग दिखाती है; खाली (निःशब्द क्रिया) खाली विभाग दिखाती है। सम पहली मात्रा और सबसे ज़ोरदार बिंदु है। खाली ऐसी जगह रखी जाती है कि भारी और खाली में अर्थपूर्ण अंतर बने और कोई हिस्सा बहुत लंबा न खिंचे। खाल…

2155.tx: बोल ऐसे भरे जाते हैं कि ताल का स्वभाव दिखे; ठेका ताल की 'पहली बंदिश' है और इसे विभाग और ताली-खाली का कड़ाई से पालन करना चाहिए, ताकि सुनने वाला ठेके से ताल पहचान ले।

2156.tx: 'दिन' और 'तिटकतगदिगन' जैसे बोल खुले बाज (पखावज से प्रेरित ताल) की ओर इशारा करते हैं; ऐसे ताल बंद बाज में अच्छे नहीं लगते। बाकी ठेके ज़रूरत के हिसाब से किसी भी बाज में बज सकते हैं।

2157.tx: भाव (शास्त्रीय, उपशास्त्रीय, सुगम) से बोल और निकास चुने जाते हैं; एक ताल के कई ठेके हो सकते हैं (जैसे तिलवाड़ा 16 मात्रा का, तीनताल के विभाग वाला ठेका है), पर कोई ठेका ताल की सीमा नहीं तोड़ सकता। सिद्धांत 5: दश प्राण और लय का आधार

2158.tx: दस प्राण (काल, मार्ग, क्रिया, अंग, ग्रह, जाति, कला, लय, यति, प्रस्तार) ताल का शास्त्रीय आधार हैं। पुराने संगीत में हर नई ताल को दसों का पालन करना होता था; आज के हिंदुस्तानी संगीत में ग्रह, जाति, लय, यति और प्रस्तार सबसे ज़्यादा काम आते हैं। ताल अपनी लय के ल…

2194.tx: Give biography of any two artists with their contribution for sangeet. 1) U. Abid Hussain 2) U. Vajid Hussain 3) U. Shammu Khan 4) Pt. Govind Barhanpurkar 5) Pt. Parvat Sinh 6) Pt. Ayodhya Prasad

2195.tx: All six are given from your notes (Biographies, VP-11). Best choices: Ut. Abid Hussain and Pt. Govindrao Burhanpurkar, which have the most detail. 1) Ustad Abid Hussain (Lucknow gharana)

2196.tx: Birth and family: born 1867 in Mehmood Ganj, Lucknow; son of Ut. Mohammad Khan, a renowned musician and associate of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. Training: learnt from his father from the age of 7, and also from his elder brother Ut. Bade Munne Khan.

2197.tx: Career: taught tabla at Marris Music College, Lucknow (now Bhatkhande Hindustani Sangeet Mahavidyalaya); for a long time accompanied the famous Kathak dancer Pt. Thakur Prasad; khalifa of the Lucknow gharana.

2198.tx: Style: powerful and sparkling (tejasvi) presentation in the khula baaj of Lucknow, suited to Kathak accompaniment. Students: his son-in-law Ut. Wajid Hussain, Pt. Biru Mishra of Banaras, Shri Hirendra Kumar Ganguli of Kolkata, Jahangir Khan; he also taught …

2199.tx: 2) Ustad Wajid Hussain (Lucknow gharana) Birth and family: born 1906 in Lucknow; son of Ut. Bade Munne Khan; son-in-law of Ut. Abid Hussain. Training: from his father from the age of 8, and from khalifa Ut. Abid Hussain Khan.

2200.tx: Style: very attractive performance with balance between tabla and bayan; ended with gat, paran, rela, tihai and chakradhar; his compositions were usually straight in structure. His gat, gat-paran and rela created a 'rav' (flow), a unique mark of his playing…

2201.tx: Position and students: khalifa of the Lucknow gharana; taught his son Ut. Afaq Hussain Khan. 3) Ustad Shammu (Shambhu) Khan (Ajrada gharana) Birth: 1876, Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh; called 'Munshi' by his family.

2202.tx: Training and work: learnt from his father and helped spread the Ajrada baaj (band baaj, tisra jati kaydas, bayan-rich playing). Student: his son Ut. Habibuddin Khan, who became one of the greatest names of Ajrada. Death: 1935. (Your notes have only this muc…

2203.tx: 4) Pt. Govindrao Burhanpurkar (pakhawaj and tabla) Birth and place: resident of Burhanpur (Nimad, Madhya Pradesh), hence 'Burhanpurkar'. Training: pakhawaj from Shri Sakharamji, a disciple of Pt. Nanasaheb Panse; dhrupad-dhamar singing from Shri Harihar Bua…

2204.tx: Career: came into contact with Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar and toured India and abroad (Burma, Ceylon) presenting pakhawaj and tabla; HMV recorded his playing during dancer Uday Shankar's performance. Books: Mridang aur Tabla Vadan Subodh and Bharatiya Taa…

2205.tx: Honours: 'Mridangacharya' (1929), award of the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, felicitation by President Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Death: 20 June 1957. 5) Pt. Parvat Singh (pakhawaj, Gwalior) Birth and family: born 1879 at Gwalior; grandfather Jorawar Singh and father …

2206.tx: Career: spent his childhood preserving and developing pakhawaj; stayed 15 years in Mumbai, accompanying many artists; after his father's death returned to Gwalior and in 1917 became pakhawaj player of the Gwalior palace.

2207.tx: Style and honours: commendable command over laya and taal; honoured as 'Vidyakala Visharad' in 1926 by the Darbhanga Naresh, president of Bharat Dharma Mandal. His son Shri Madhav Singh also had the Gwalior court's support. Death: 18 July 1951. 6) Pt. Ayodh…

2208.tx: Birth and family: born 5 August 1891 at Datia (Madhya Pradesh); his father Pt. Gaya Prasad was a famous mridang player. Training: mridang from Shri Ram Singh and his father Pt. Gaya Prasad; dhrupad singing from Ut. Vazir Khan and Nawab Chhamman Khan.

2209.tx: Career: performed for many years on Akashvani and at sangeet sammelans; spent several years in Rampur. Style: a renowned mridang player for his command over layakari; Chautaal was one of his favourite taals. Honour and death: Padma Shri from the Government …

2230.ti: Tabla / pakhawaj accompaniment in classical, semi-classical and light music
2230.tx: The main artist chooses raga, taal and laya; the tabla must be tuned exactly. Keep the laya undisturbed and change it only on the artist's signal; keep taali-khaali clear so the singer can always find the taal.

2231.ti: Tabla / pakhawaj accompaniment in classical, semi-classical and light music

2241.tx: Qualities of a good accompanist: imagination, observation and intelligence; regular listening to all styles; no ego; sensitivity to soft and hard sounds. Ut. Alla Rakha and Ut. Habibuddin Khan were celebrated accompanists.

2242.ti: Tabla / pakhawaj accompaniment in classical, semi-classical and light music
2242.tx: Conclusion: The basic rule is the same in all three forms: follow the main artist, keep the laya and mood, and never disturb the singer's idea. Only the amount of freedom changes: least in classical, most in light music.

2396.ti: Classification of Indian instruments; relation between avanaddha and ghana
2396.tx: Ghana keeps the beat, avanaddha gives the bols: manjira or kartal mark the taali points simply, while the drum fills the theka with bols; the ghana instrument helps the drum keep steady laya.

2397.ti: Classification of Indian instruments; relation between avanaddha and ghana
2397.tx: History: both are among the oldest instruments: bhoomi-dundubhi (avanaddha) and clappers/bells (ghana) go back to the Vedic period; both are classed together as 'taal vadya'.

2398.ti: Classification of Indian instruments; relation between avanaddha and ghana
2398.tx: Conclusion: Indian instruments are tat, sushir, avanaddha and ghana. Avanaddha and ghana are partners: both keep taal, one through a skin and bols, the other through the solid body itself, and they often play together.

2459.tx: Conclusion: In solo playing the kayada builds the expansion, the rela brings speed, and the gat (or, on pakhawaj, the gat paran and chakradhar paran) crowns the solo with fixed compositions of beauty; this order follows the rise of laya from madhya to drut.

2482.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2482.tx: One possible order (it may change with gharana and baaj): uthan / peshkar → kaydas → relas → gat → tukda → chakradhar → farmaishi chakradhar → kamaali chakradhar → paran → tihai. Stage · What is played · How it should be ·

2483.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2483.tx: Opening (vilambit) · Peshkar (Banaras: uthan) · Bound to the taal, showing vibhag and khaali-bhari; alapchari; each variation grows from the previous one; ends on a vowel bol. The most improvisational part: shows maturity and gharana. ·

2484.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2484.tx: Expansion (madhya) · Kaydas · Mukh, paltas only from the mukh's bols, khaali-bhari, tihai; clear bols, steady laya. · Speed (madhya → drut) · Relas, rau · Unbroken chain of fast bols ending on a consonant; even strokes, stamina. ·

2485.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2485.tx: Fixed compositions (drut) · Gat, tukda, chakradhar, paran · Recited first (padhant), then played; a varied collection so that different concerts sound different. · Ending · Tihai · A strong landing on sam; then thanks to the audience. ·

2486.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2486.tx: The order goes from most expandable (peshkar) to less expandable (kayda, rela) to fixed, and from most improvisable (new bols allowed in peshkar) to less improvisable (no new bols in kayda). Most improvisation happens in the first half, where the slower lay…

2488.tx: Fixed compositions are recited aloud before playing, mentioning the composer's name respectfully, with taali-khaali on the hand. Clear recitation even at fast speed makes the presentation attractive; it helps memory, shows the weight (vazan) of the bols, gi…

2489.tx: 4) Qualities of an effective solo Finish within the time given by the organisers; humility and a calm stage presence. A large repertoire; command over laya and layakari; new tihai patterns and prastar that show the player's own thinking.

2490.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2490.tx: Balance of power and nazakat (delicacy): playing powerfully with willpower is not the same as making as much noise as possible. Knowledge of gharana, baaj and nikas: each composition played in its own style. Watch the instrument's tuning and the audience's …

2492.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2492.tx: The pakhawaj solo follows the same principles with its own repertoire: after the theka, relas of fast bols, then fixed parans (gat paran, stuti paran, aadeshi/farmaishi paran) and chakradhar parans with open, forceful bols played with the whole palm, ending…

2493.ti: How the playing should be in a tabla / pakhawaj solo
2493.tx: Conclusion: A good solo is all-round: it begins with respect, moves from vilambit to drut and from expandable to fixed compositions, uses clear padhant, balances power with delicacy, and ends on time with a strong tihai on sam.

2508.ti: Accompaniment for classical, semi-classical and light music
2508.tx: Sangat means supporting the main artist on tabla or pakhawaj. The accompanist gives the singer a steady 'zameen' (ground) on which to build his creativity; he is a helper, not the master. The tabla's low bayan note and high dayan note let it accompany khaya…

2509.ti: Accompaniment for classical, semi-classical and light music
2509.tx: The main artist chooses raga, taal and laya; the tabla must be tuned exactly. Keep the laya undisturbed and change it only on the artist's signal; keep taali-khaali clear so the singer can always find the taal.

2510.ti: Accompaniment for classical, semi-classical and light music
2510.tx: Pieces should be neither bland nor excessive; never disturb the singer's line of thought; suit the time and mood of the raga. Play small pieces only with permission and return to theka; accompaniment should not look like a 'collage'. 1) Classical singing

2520.ti: Accompaniment for classical, semi-classical and light music
2520.tx: Qualities of a good accompanist: imagination, observation and intelligence; regular listening to all styles; no ego; sensitivity to soft and hard sounds. Ut. Alla Rakha and Ut. Habibuddin Khan were celebrated accompanists.

2521.ti: Accompaniment for classical, semi-classical and light music
2521.tx: Conclusion: The basic rule is the same in all three forms: follow the main artist, keep the laya and mood, and never disturb the singer's idea. Only the amount of freedom changes: least in classical, most in light music.

2591.tx: Introduction: Khalifa (torchbearer) of the Delhi gharana; born in 1875 in Delhi; died in 1940. Training: learnt from his father Ut. Bolibaksh Khan; did enormous riyaz, said to be 16–18 hours a day.

2592.tx: Style: kaydas with dhatit and DRDR at very fast speed, including a two-finger DRDR kayda, always with aesthetic expression; balance of tabla and bayan; an 'aasdaar' (resonant, strong) sound; clear nikas and the right weight of every bol.

2593.tx: Contribution: preserved the Delhi baaj; several recordings survive. Showed two different nikas for the same kayda. Disciples: Ut. Habibuddin Khan (Ajrada), Hirendra Kishor, Raj Chaudhari, Keshav Chandra Banerjee. 2) Ustad Shammu (Shambhu) Khan (Ajrada gharana)

2594.tx: Introduction: born in 1876 in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh; a tabla player of the Ajrada gharana; called 'Munshi' in his family; died in 1935. Training: learnt tabla from his father.

2595.tx: Style and gharana: the Ajrada baaj: a bandh baaj with the ring finger added for speed, tisra jati kaydas, a sweet, expressive bayan with meend and gheeskam.

2596.tx: Contribution: helped spread the Ajrada baaj. His son and student Ut. Habibuddin Khan became the most famous Ajrada player. (Your notes have only this much; choose him only if you can add more from your guru.) 3) Pandit Ayodhya Prasad (Pakhawaj, Kudau Singh …

2598.tx: Style: renowned for command over layakari; Chautaal was a favourite taal. Contribution and honours: performed for many years on Akashvani and at music conferences; awarded the Padma Shri. 4) Pandit Parvat Singh (Pakhawaj, Gwalior)

2599.tx: Introduction: born in 1879 in Gwalior; grandfather Jorawar Singh and father Sukhdev Singh were senior artists of the Gwalior court; died on 18 July 1951.

2600.tx: Career: spent his childhood preserving and enriching pakhawaj; lived 15 years in Mumbai accompanying many artists; returned to Gwalior after his father's death and in 1917 became the pakhawaj player of the Gwalior palace.

2602.tx: Birth and family: born 1867 in Mehmood Ganj, Lucknow; son of Ut. Mohammad Khan, a renowned musician and associate of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. Training: learnt from his father from the age of 7, and also from his elder brother Ut. Bade Munne Khan.

2603.tx: Career: taught tabla at Marris Music College, Lucknow (now Bhatkhande Hindustani Sangeet Mahavidyalaya); for a long time accompanied the famous Kathak dancer Pt. Thakur Prasad; khalifa of the Lucknow gharana.

2604.tx: Style: powerful and sparkling (tejasvi) presentation in the khula baaj of Lucknow, suited to Kathak accompaniment. Students: his son-in-law Ut. Wajid Hussain, Pt. Biru Mishra of Banaras, Shri Hirendra Kumar Ganguli of Kolkata, Jahangir Khan; he also taught …

2606.tx: Training: pakhawaj first from his father, then from Shri Kotadikar, who served the royal family at Pune; then 12 years of study at Kashi; settled in Indore. ⚑ The 2024 online paper key calls him a disciple of Kudau Singh; your notes do not say this.

2607.tx: Contribution: with royal support at Indore he changed pakhawaj performance: by studying the literature and applying mathematics he composed many parans and new thekas (the Sudarshan theka is his), and created a simpler teaching method bound in matras, with …

2751.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2751.tx: In Bharat Muni's classification, the tanpura is a tat (stringed) instrument, while the dholak and sambal are avanaddha (membrane) instruments. For each, write the type, structure (with a simple sketch), how it is played and where it is used. a) Tanpura (tat)

2752.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2752.tx: Type and names: a long-necked stringed (tat) instrument; also called tambura; a smaller version, the tanpuri, accompanies sitar and sarod. Role: it does not play a melody; it keeps a continuous harmonic drone that sustains the singer's or instrumentalist's …

2753.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2753.tx: Playing: usually four strings are plucked one after another in a continuous cycle; their tones blend with one another and with the singer's voice.

2754.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2754.tx: Size and tuning: tanpuras come in different sizes to suit the artist's pitch: male singers usually use large ones, women singers smaller ones; the tonic Sa of the singer decides the pitch, and the string pattern depends on the raga.

2755.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2755.tx: Use and importance: classical vocal and instrumental music; hailed as an Indian instrument with a remarkable effect on the singer's intonation. b) Dholak (avanaddha)

2756.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2756.tx: Structure: a horizontal cylindrical drum with two faces; the larger face is buffalo hide with a paste (shahi) for a deeper pitch, the smaller face goat hide for sharper notes. Playing: with the hands; played sitting, or standing with a rope round the neck; …

2757.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2757.tx: Use: a very popular folk instrument: qawwali, lavani, kirtan, bhangra, ghazal and light music; also processions, weddings and festivals. Taals: Keherwa, Dadra. Related: the dholki (naal) of Maharashtra is a smaller version, used in tamasha and lavani. c) Sa…

2758.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2758.tx: Structure: a set of two drums joined together with faces on top: the smaller, higher-pitched one of wood, the larger of brass. Playing: hung from the waist with a cord and played standing, with two wooden sticks with bent tips (one almost circular).

2759.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2759.tx: Use: Maharashtra: gondhal in honour of Goddess Tulja Bhavani, Ganapati visarjan and religious processions (a past MCQ: 'instrument played in gondhal' = sambal).

2760.ti: Tanpura, dholak and sambal in detail
2760.tx: Conclusion: The tanpura gives the swar base and the dholak and sambal give rhythm: the tanpura belongs to classical music, the dholak to folk and light music, and the sambal to Maharashtra's devotional and festive music.

2776.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2776.tx: Structure of the taal: Bhatkhande clearly shows sam, every taali, khaali and every vibhag. Paluskar shows sam, taali and khaali but not the vibhag, because the line comes only at the end.

2777.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2777.tx: Position of the taali: in Bhatkhande we read the taali's serial number, so we must count to find which matra it falls on. In Paluskar the matra number itself is written, so the position is read directly.

2778.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2778.tx: Value of each bol: Bhatkhande puts one arc under any matra with many bols, so we cannot tell how the matra was divided; for example a tisra 1/6 and a chatusra 1/8 look the same. Paluskar gives each bol its own duration sign, so the jati of every matra is cl…

2779.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2779.tx: Limits: Paluskar has no sign for 1/5 or 1/7 of a matra, so Kuaad and Biaad cannot be shown properly in it. Bhatkhande can express every jati, which is why papers ask for Kuaad/Biaad in Bhatkhande notation.

2780.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2780.tx: Speed of writing: Bhatkhande is quicker and simpler, so it is preferred for long compositions. Paluskar takes more time but is better for showing jati and small layakaris such as tigun and chaugun. Use today: Bhatkhande notation is more widely used in North…

2781.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation: detail, merits and demerits, one taal in both
2781.tx: Conclusion: Both systems have advantages and limits. Bhatkhande is fast and shows the taal's structure (vibhag, taali, khaali) clearly; Paluskar is slower but shows the exact value and jati of each bol. A good student should be able to write in both. Part B…

2818.ti: Kriya, jati and yati in detail
2818.tx: Conclusion: Kriya shows the taal's structure by hand (today's taali-khaali), jati decides how a matra is divided, and yati decides how laya flows through a composition. All three remain alive in today's tabla playing and accompaniment.

2909.ti: One gharana in detail, point by point
2909.tx: Conclusion: Farrukhabad grew from Lucknow's open baaj into the most complete school of tabla, joining the gat and chakradhar of the khula baaj with the peshkar, kayda and rela of Delhi; its composers' gats are still played in every solo.

2923.ti: Accompaniment with semi-classical or light music, with examples
2923.tx: Sangat means supporting the main artist on tabla or pakhawaj. The accompanist gives the singer a steady 'zameen' (ground) on which to build his creativity; he is a helper, not the master. The tabla's low bayan note and high dayan note let it accompany khaya…

2924.ti: Accompaniment with semi-classical or light music, with examples
2924.tx: The main artist chooses raga, taal and laya; the tabla must be tuned exactly. Keep the laya undisturbed and change it only on the artist's signal; keep taali-khaali clear so the singer can always find the taal.

2925.ti: Accompaniment with semi-classical or light music, with examples
2925.tx: Pieces should be neither bland nor excessive; never disturb the singer's line of thought; suit the time and mood of the raga. Play small pieces only with permission and return to theka; accompaniment should not look like a 'collage'. 1) Classical singing

2935.ti: Accompaniment with semi-classical or light music, with examples
2935.tx: Qualities of a good accompanist: imagination, observation and intelligence; regular listening to all styles; no ego; sensitivity to soft and hard sounds. Ut. Alla Rakha and Ut. Habibuddin Khan were celebrated accompanists.

2936.ti: Accompaniment with semi-classical or light music, with examples
2936.tx: Conclusion: The basic rule is the same in all three forms: follow the main artist, keep the laya and mood, and never disturb the singer's idea. Only the amount of freedom changes: least in classical, most in light music.

2953.tx: All six are given from your notes (Biographies). Tabla students: best choices are Ut. Natthu Khan and Ut. Chudiyawale Imam Bakhsh. Tabla 1) Ustad Chudiyawale Imam Bakhsh (Farrukhabad gharana)

2954.tx: Introduction: a famous exponent of the Farrukhabad gharana; his birth and death dates are not recorded. Between about 1850 and 1875 he often accompanied the famous Gwalior singers Ut. Hassu Khan and Ut. Haddu Khan.

2955.tx: Training: he first played pakhawaj. He then served Ut. Haji Vilayat Ali Khan for several years as his hukka attendant, picked up many tabla skills, and was generously accepted as his disciple. He also learnt a great deal from Haji Saheb's wife, Moti Bibi, w…

2956.tx: Why 'Chudiyawale': at his ganda-bandhan ceremony Moti Bibi tied a bangle (chudi) on his wrist instead of the usual thread; hence the name. Contribution: composed and popularised many tabla compositions that are still played; one of the senior disciples who …

2957.tx: Family: his son was Ut. Haider Bakhsh. Tabla 2) Ustad Shammu (Shambhu) Khan (Ajrada gharana) Introduction: born in 1876 in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh; a tabla player of the Ajrada gharana; called 'Munshi' in his family; died in 1935. Training: learnt ta…

2958.tx: Style and gharana: the Ajrada baaj: a bandh baaj with the ring finger added for speed, tisra jati kaydas, a sweet, expressive bayan with meend and gheeskam.

2959.tx: Contribution: helped spread the Ajrada baaj. His son and student Ut. Habibuddin Khan became the most famous Ajrada player. (Your notes have only this much; choose him only if you can add more from your guru.) Tabla 3) Ustad Natthu Khan (Delhi gharana)

2960.tx: Introduction: Khalifa (torchbearer) of the Delhi gharana; born in 1875 in Delhi; died in 1940. Training: learnt from his father Ut. Bolibaksh Khan; did enormous riyaz, said to be 16–18 hours a day.

2961.tx: Style: kaydas with dhatit and DRDR at very fast speed, including a two-finger DRDR kayda, always with aesthetic expression; balance of tabla and bayan; an 'aasdaar' (resonant, strong) sound; clear nikas and the right weight of every bol.

2962.tx: Contribution: preserved the Delhi baaj; several recordings survive. Showed two different nikas for the same kayda. Disciples: Ut. Habibuddin Khan (Ajrada), Hirendra Kishor, Raj Chaudhari, Keshav Chandra Banerjee. Pakhawaj 1) Pandit Ayodhya Prasad (Pakhawaj,…

2963.tx: Introduction: born on 5 August 1891 in Datia (MP); son of the famous mridang player Pt. Gaya Prasad; died on 18 December 1977. Training: mridang from Shri Ram Singh and his father; dhrupad singing from Ut. Vazir Khan and Nawab Chhamman Khan; spent several y…

2964.tx: Style: renowned for command over layakari; Chautaal was a favourite taal. Contribution and honours: performed for many years on Akashvani and at music conferences; awarded the Padma Shri. Pakhawaj 2) Pandit Parvat Singh (Pakhawaj, Gwalior)

2965.tx: Introduction: born in 1879 in Gwalior; grandfather Jorawar Singh and father Sukhdev Singh were senior artists of the Gwalior court; died on 18 July 1951.

2966.tx: Career: spent his childhood preserving and enriching pakhawaj; lived 15 years in Mumbai accompanying many artists; returned to Gwalior after his father's death and in 1917 became the pakhawaj player of the Gwalior palace.

2967.tx: Style and honours: commendable command over laya and taal; honoured as 'Vidyakala Visharad' in 1926 by the Darbhanga Naresh (president of Bharat Dharma Mandal). His son Madhav Singh was also supported by the Gwalior court. Pakhawaj 3) Pt. Govindrao Burhanpu…

2968.tx: Birth and place: resident of Burhanpur (Nimad, Madhya Pradesh), hence 'Burhanpurkar'. Training: pakhawaj from Shri Sakharamji, a disciple of Pt. Nanasaheb Panse; dhrupad-dhamar singing from Shri Harihar Bua Kopargaonkar; tabla from Pt. Vamanrao of Hyderabad.

2969.tx: Career: came into contact with Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar and toured India and abroad (Burma, Ceylon) presenting pakhawaj and tabla; HMV recorded his playing during dancer Uday Shankar's performance. Books: Mridang aur Tabla Vadan Subodh and Bharatiya Taa…

2970.tx: Honours: 'Mridangacharya' (1929), award of the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, felicitation by President Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Death: 20 June 1957.

3017.tx: Write an essay in your own words on any one of the following: 1. Ideal riyaz in the art of tabla / pakhawaj playing 2. Padhant, a necessity 3. Tabla / pakhawaj playing: present condition. (translated; the paper is in Hindi only)

3018.tx: Topics 1 and 2 are written in full from your notes; write either one. Topic 3 is not covered in your notes. Essay 1: Ideal riyaz in tabla / pakhawaj Introduction

3019.tx: Riyaz is regular, disciplined practice. The tabla is a pair: the dayan (right hand) gives clear bol-nikas, tite/tirakita, layakari and speed; the bayan (left hand) gives meend, ghumak and an open, resonant naad. Ideal riyaz trains both hands equally, so tha…

3020.tx: Ideal practice methods Fixed time every day: practise at a set time daily; regularity makes the hand 'riyazi'. Slow to fast: start in thah and move thah → dugun → tigun → chaugun, keeping every bol clear and the wrist relaxed; speed must never break the bols.

3021.tx: Both hands equally (dayan-bayan balance): practise the same bol or kayda with both hands together, so that every Dha sounds the same.

3022.tx: Correct nikas, right hand: Dha/Ta with the index finger straight on the chanti, vertical movement of about 1–1½ inches; tite with two fingers in the middle of the syahi (practice phrase 'dhatidhati… dhitedhite'); tirakita with all four letters evenly spaced…

3023.tx: Correct nikas, left hand: keep the whole hand on the bayan (not just the wrist); ghe-ghe with a vertical pull and release; practise meend and the open naad after Dha/Dhin. Naad awareness: know soft and hard sounds; playing loudly is not the goal; strength a…

3024.tx: Tuning: keep the dayan tuned to the lehra's Sa; practising on an out-of-tune tabla spoils the ear. Padhant with riyaz: recite the bols while showing taali-khaali; it fixes the composition in memory, teaches the weight of bols and builds confidence.

3025.tx: Kayda riyaz — murakka and chilla ⚑: murakka = repeating one kayda again and again until it plays effortlessly; chilla = a fixed period (traditionally 40 days) of long, strict, solitary daily practice. (Your notes give these names; the definitions are the tr…

3026.tx: Repertoire and layakari: build a large collection of compositions of different gharanas, and practise different layakaris and taals. Example of a great artist's riyaz

3027.tx: Ut. Ahmedjan Thirakwa (Farrukhabad) learnt for 26 years from Ut. Munir Khan, who gave him the baaj of four gharanas. His hand became 'riyazi' through 14–15 hours of practice a day; it was said that his tabla satisfied listeners like singing. Ut. Natthu Khan…

3028.tx: Conclusion: Ideal riyaz is regular, at a fixed time, slow to fast, with both hands balanced, correct nikas, awareness of naad, a tuned instrument and padhant. Strength and nazakat both come only from such daily discipline. Essay 2: Padhant, a necessity

3029.tx: Introduction: padhant is the recitation of tabla or pakhawaj bols aloud while showing taali and khaali on the hand. Students do it from the first day; in a concert, fixed compositions are recited by respectfully naming the composer and then reciting the com…

3030.tx: Memory: padhant fixes taals and compositions in memory; compositions of masters are passed on with their correct pronunciation and origin.

3031.tx: Weight (vazan) of bols: repeating a composition aloud, just as it will be played, reveals its hidden weights and intricacies, and shows how to express it beautifully; this gradually passes into the hands. Laya and taal: reciting with taali-khaali trains the…

3032.tx: Confidence and expression: it gives self-confidence and brings life to the composition when it is played.

3033.tx: Presentation: clear padhant even at fast speed, practised slow to fast, makes the presentation of fixed compositions attractive; with a short description it tells the audience what to listen for and helps them enjoy it.

3034.tx: Kathak: in Kathak the dancer recites parans and the tabla or pakhawaj plays them as they are, so padhant links dancer and accompanist.

3035.tx: Conclusion: Padhant is not an extra; it is part of riyaz and of performance. It helps memory, reveals the weight of bols, steadies the laya, builds confidence and lets the audience enjoy the composition.

3145.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative
3145.tx: Structure of the taal: Bhatkhande clearly shows sam, every taali, khaali and every vibhag. Paluskar shows sam, taali and khaali but not the vibhag, because the line comes only at the end.

3146.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative
3146.tx: Position of the taali: in Bhatkhande we read the taali's serial number, so we must count to find which matra it falls on. In Paluskar the matra number itself is written, so the position is read directly.

3147.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative
3147.tx: Value of each bol: Bhatkhande puts one arc under any matra with many bols, so we cannot tell how the matra was divided; for example a tisra 1/6 and a chatusra 1/8 look the same. Paluskar gives each bol its own duration sign, so the jati of every matra is cl…

3148.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative
3148.tx: Limits: Paluskar has no sign for 1/5 or 1/7 of a matra, so Kuaad and Biaad cannot be shown properly in it. Bhatkhande can express every jati, which is why papers ask for Kuaad/Biaad in Bhatkhande notation.

3149.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative
3149.tx: Speed of writing: Bhatkhande is quicker and simpler, so it is preferred for long compositions. Paluskar takes more time but is better for showing jati and small layakaris such as tigun and chaugun. Use today: Bhatkhande notation is more widely used in North…

3150.ti: Bhatkhande and Paluskar notation systems: detailed and comparative

3204.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3204.tx: Name the ten pranas of taal in order and explain 'graha' and 'yati' in brief. (translated; the paper is in Hindi only)

3205.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3205.tx: The ten pranas in order The ten basic characteristics of taal, the dash pran ('breath of life'), are described in Sangeet Ratnakar by Sharangdev (about 13th century), in this order: काल मार्ग क्रियाङ्गानि ग्रहो जाति: कला लय: । यति: प्रस्तारकश्चेति तालप्राणा…

3206.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3206.tx: 1. Kaal · Time, or the passing of time; felt in one cycle, from start to end of a composition, and between vibhags. Natya Shastra: the time to say 'ka cha ta ta pa'. ·

3207.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3207.tx: 2. Marg · The 'path' of the taal, used in margi taals. Four margs: Dhruva (1 beat: Dhruvaka), Chitra (2: + Sarpini), Vartika (4: + Krishna, Padmini), Dakshina (8: + Visarjita, Vikshipta, Pataka, Patita). ·

3208.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3208.tx: 3. Kriya · Showing taal with hand actions. Sashabd: Dhruva, Shamya, Taal, Sannipat. Nishabd: Avap, Nishkram, Vikshep, Praveshak. Today: taali (sashabd) and khaali (nishabd). · 4. Ang · Parts of a taal: Anudrut 1, Drut 2, Laghu 4, Guru 8, Pluta 12, Kakapada …

3209.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3209.tx: 5. Graha · Where the song begins relative to the taal ('paani'): sam (together), atit (taal before song), anagat (taal after song). · 6. Jati · Division of a matra: tisra 3, chatusra 4, khand 5, mishra 7, sankirna 9. Carnatic: 7 suladi taals × 5 jatis = 35;…

3210.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3210.tx: 7. Kala · The art of showing the time-span with graceful hand and body movements while playing (Dhruvaka, Sarpini, Krishna, Padmini, Visarjita, Vikshipta, Pataka, Patita). · 8. Laya · The rest after a kriya; the steady gap between two matras: vilambit, madh…

3211.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3211.tx: 9. Yati · The flow of laya: Sama (same throughout), Srotogata (slow → fast, like a river), Gopuchha (fast → slow, like a cow's tail), Mridanga (madhya → vilambit → drut), Pipilika (irregular, like an ant). ·

3212.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3212.tx: 10. Prastar · Permutations of the parts of a taal (vistar); e.g. 4 beats as 3+1, 1+3, 2+2, 2+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 1+1+1+1. Root of paltas and upaj. · Ancient (margi) music required all ten for any taal; today Hindustani music mainly uses graha, jati, laya, ya…

3213.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3213.tx: Graha tells where a song or composition begins in relation to sam (the 'paani'). There are three kinds: Graha · Where it begins · Meaning · Sam graha · Exactly on sam: song and taal start together · 'Same' · Atit graha · A little after sam: the taal starts …

3214.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3214.tx: Anagat graha · A little before sam: the song starts before the taal's sam · 'Anagat' = not yet come; sam is still to come ·

3215.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3215.tx: Graha matters in accompaniment: the tabla player must know on which syllable of the bandish sam falls, because singers often begin a composition before or after sam (a mukhda that starts before sam and lands on it is anagat). Yati

3216.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3216.tx: Yati is the set of rules for the flow of laya through a composition: how the laya moves from beginning to end. Yati · Flow of laya · Image · Sama · Same at beginning, middle and end · Level ground · Srotogata · Slow → fast (vilambit → madhya → drut) · A riv…

3217.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3217.tx: Gopuchha · Fast → slow (drut → madhya → vilambit) · A cow's tail · Mridanga · Madhya → vilambit → drut · Shape of the mridang · Pipilika · Irregular: vilambit → madhya → vilambit, or madhya → drut → madhya · The gait of an ant · A tabla solo normally follow…

3218.ti: The ten pranas in order; graha and yati in brief
3218.tx: Conclusion: Of the ten pranas, graha decides where a composition begins in relation to sam and yati decides how its laya flows; both remain alive in today's singing, solo and accompaniment.

3219.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3219.tx: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमश: बताईये तथा 'ग्रह' एवं 'यति' को संक्षेप में समझाईये।

3220.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3220.tx: दस प्राण क्रम से ताल की दस मूल विशेषताएँ, दश प्राण ('जीवन की साँस'), शारंगदेव के संगीत रत्नाकर (लगभग 13वीं सदी) में इस क्रम में बताई गई हैं: काल मार्ग क्रियाङ्गानि ग्रहो जाति: कला लय: । यति: प्रस्तारकश्चेति तालप्राणा दशस्मृता: ॥ प्राण · अर्थ और विवरण ·

3221.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3221.tx: 1. काल · समय, या समय का बीतना; एक आवर्तन में, रचना के आरंभ से अंत तक, और विभागों के बीच महसूस होता है। नाट्यशास्त्र: 'क च ट त प' बोलने का समय। ·

3222.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3222.tx: 2. मार्ग · ताल का 'रास्ता', मार्गी तालों में। चार मार्ग: ध्रुव (1 बीट: ध्रुवका), चित्र (2: + सर्पिणी), वार्तिक (4: + कृष्णा, पद्मिनी), दक्षिण (8: + विसर्जिता, विक्षिप्ता, पताका, पतिता)। ·

3223.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3223.tx: 3. क्रिया · हाथ की क्रिया से ताल दिखाना। सशब्द: ध्रुवा, शम्या, ताल, सन्निपात। निःशब्द: आवाप, निष्क्राम, विक्षेप, प्रवेशक। आज: ताली (सशब्द) और खाली (निःशब्द)। · 4. अंग · ताल के हिस्से: अणुद्रुत 1, द्रुत 2, लघु 4, गुरु 8, प्लुत 12, काकपद 16 (देशी मान, मूल का …

3224.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3224.tx: 5. ग्रह · ताल के मुकाबले गीत कहाँ से शुरू ('पाणि'): सम (साथ), अतीत (ताल पहले), अनागत (ताल बाद में)। · 6. जाति · मात्रा का बँटवारा: तिस्र 3, चतुरस्र 4, खंड 5, मिश्र 7, संकीर्ण 9। कर्नाटक: 7 सूलादि ताल × 5 जाति = 35; × 5 गति = 175। ·

3225.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3225.tx: 7. कला · बजाते समय हाथ और शरीर की सुंदर गतियों से समय दिखाने की कला (ध्रुवका, सर्पिणी, कृष्णा, पद्मिनी, विसर्जिता, विक्षिप्ता, पताका, पतिता)। · 8. लय · क्रिया के बाद का विश्राम; दो मात्राओं के बीच का एक-सा अंतर: विलंबित, मध्य, द्रुत। ·

3226.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3226.tx: 9. यति · लय का बहाव: समा (एक-सी), स्रोतोगता (धीमे से तेज़, नदी जैसी), गोपुच्छा (तेज़ से धीमे, गाय की पूँछ जैसी), मृदंगा (मध्य → विलंबित → द्रुत), पिपीलिका (टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी, चींटी जैसी)। · 10. प्रस्तार · ताल के हिस्सों के क्रमचय (विस्तार); जैसे 4 बीट = 3+1, 1+3,…

3227.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3227.tx: प्राचीन (मार्गी) संगीत में हर ताल के लिए दसों ज़रूरी थे; आज हिंदुस्तानी संगीत मुख्य रूप से ग्रह, जाति, लय, यति और प्रस्तार का प्रयोग करता है। ग्रह ग्रह बताता है कि गीत या रचना सम के मुकाबले कहाँ से शुरू होती है ('पाणि')। इसके तीन प्रकार हैं: ग्रह · कहाँ से …

3228.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3228.tx: सम ग्रह · ठीक सम पर: गीत और ताल साथ शुरू · 'समान' · अतीत ग्रह · सम के थोड़ा बाद: ताल गीत से पहले शुरू · 'अतीत' = बीता हुआ; सम निकल चुका · अनागत ग्रह · सम के थोड़ा पहले: गीत ताल के सम से पहले शुरू · 'अनागत' = अभी नहीं आया; सम आने वाला है ·

3229.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3229.tx: संगत में ग्रह ज़रूरी है: तबला वादक को पता होना चाहिए कि बंदिश के किस अक्षर पर सम है, क्योंकि गायक अक्सर रचना सम से पहले या बाद शुरू करते हैं (सम से पहले शुरू होकर सम पर आने वाला मुखड़ा अनागत है)। यति यति रचना में लय के बहाव के नियम हैं: आरंभ से अंत तक लय कै…

3230.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3230.tx: समा · आरंभ, बीच और अंत में एक-सी · समतल ज़मीन · स्रोतोगता · धीमी → तेज़ (विलंबित → मध्य → द्रुत) · नदी जो पानी बढ़ने पर तेज़ बहती है · गोपुच्छा · तेज़ → धीमी (द्रुत → मध्य → विलंबित) · गाय की पूँछ · मृदंगा · मध्य → विलंबित → द्रुत · मृदंग का आकार ·

3231.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3231.tx: पिपीलिका · टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी: विलंबित → मध्य → विलंबित, या मध्य → द्रुत → मध्य · चींटी की चाल · तबला एकल आमतौर पर स्रोतोगता यति में चलता है (पेशकार → कायदा → रेला → तुकड़ा)।

3232.ti: ताल के दश प्राणों के नाम क्रमशः; ग्रह और यति संक्षेप में
3232.tx: निष्कर्ष: दस प्राणों में ग्रह तय करता है कि रचना सम के मुकाबले कहाँ से शुरू हो और यति तय करती है कि उसकी लय कैसे बहे; दोनों आज के गायन, एकल और संगत में ज़िंदा हैं।

3283.tx: Ti / Te, Ta of TRKT (closed, syahi) · Fingers strike the syahi and stay (closed); the 'Ta' of TiRaKiTa is played with ring and little fingers. · Ki / Ke / Ka (bayan, closed) · The flat hand strikes the bayan and stays; flat, closed sound. ·

3284.tx: Ge / Ghe / Ga (bayan, open) · The whole hand rests on the bayan; the index finger, then middle and ring fingers alternately, strike the maidan with a vertical movement; open, resonant. · Da (in GDNG) · Ring and little fingers strike the outer side of the ta…

3285.tx: Dha (combined) · Na/Ta on the dayan + Ge on the bayan together. · 1) किटतक (Kittak)

3286.tx: कि = flat closed stroke on the bayan; ट = closed stroke on the syahi with ring and little fingers (as the 'Ta' of TiRaKiTa); त = closed stroke on the syahi with the index and middle fingers (like Ti); क = flat closed stroke on the bayan again. All four are …

3288.tx: त = closed stroke on the syahi; क्का = a strong flat stroke on the bayan (left face), the doubled 'kk' giving extra weight; थुं = an open, resonant stroke in the middle of the right face with the fingers (like Tun on tabla, a 'thun' on pakhawaj); गा = open …

3289.tx: 3) काऽकिट (KaSkit) का = flat closed stroke on the bayan, held for the pause ऽ; then कि = closed stroke on the bayan again and ट = closed stroke on the syahi with ring and little fingers. The pause after Ka gives the phrase its swing; all strokes are closed.…

3290.tx: त = closed stroke on the syahi; क् = flat stroke on the bayan; धे = Dhe: open Ge on the bayan together with a closed Te on the syahi, held for the pause ऽ; त्ता = a strong Ta on the chanti/kinar (doubled for weight). ⚑ 5) नगधेत् (Nagadhet) ⚑

3291.tx: न = Na with the index finger on the chanti; ग = open Ge on the bayan; धेत् = Dhet: open Ge on the bayan with a closed Te on the syahi, the final 't' cutting the sound short. ⚑ 6) घिडाऽन (GhidaSn)

3292.tx: Your notes give the nikas of घिडनग (not to be confused with गदिगन, which is played differently): घि = Ge played normally on the bayan; डा = ring and little fingers strike the outer side of the tabla on the sur, where they rest for Dha; ऽ = pause; न = played…

3293.tx: Conclusion: Every varna is built from a few basic strokes: open or closed, on the dayan, the bayan or both. Correct nikas keeps each stroke clear, the wrist loose and the dayan-bayan balanced; the same varna may be played a little differently in each gharan…

3308.tx: How a gharana is formed (origination) Among many students who play exactly like the guru, one student thinks differently, learns from other styles and creates a new style.

3309.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3309.tx: If the new style is followed for at least three generations, it is accepted as a gharana. It is usually named after the founder's town (Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farrukhabad, Banaras, Punjab).

3317.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3317.tx: Baaj: band baaj; 'do ungli ka baaj' or 'chanti ka baaj', played mainly with the index and middle fingers; Ta/Dha struck sharply on the chanti; the bayan played without lifting the hand, with little meend.

3318.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3318.tx: Compositions: peshkar, kayda and rela dominate; even the peshkar is expanded like a kayda, in the order of the mukh's bols. It is the most restrictive gharana. Kaydas are mostly chatusra jati; the kayda is presented as mukh, dohra, bal, palta, tihai; solos …

3319.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3319.tx: Bols: dhite, tite, kite, dhage, dhagena, dhinagena, two-finger DRDR. Artists: Ut. Gamme Khan (brought taals other than Teentaal into Delhi), Ut. Inam Ali Khan (last major khalifa), Ut. Natthu Khan (famous for fast two-finger DRDR kaydas). Gharana 2: Lucknow

3320.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3320.tx: Founder and origin: Ut. Modu Khan and Ut. Bakshu Khan, students of the Delhi gharana, within about 50 years of Delhi. The Nawabs of Lucknow supported Kathak, and Kathak's tatkar sounded better with tabla than with pakhawaj; so they built a new style from Ka…

3321.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3321.tx: Baaj: khula baaj, also called hatheli ka baaj, thapiya ka baaj or poorab baaj; the lav instead of the chanti on the tabla, the maidan on the bayan, and a thaap made by closing four fingers.

3322.ti: Names of tabla / pakhawaj gharanas; one gharana in detail
3322.tx: Compositions: gat, gat-paran, tukda and chakradhar dominate; kaydas are few and carry the language of gat (e.g. 'ghidan'). 'Tukda' comes from 'paran ka tukda'. Pre-composed bandishes are important, and a solo may start without a peshkar.

3357.ti: Farrukhabad or Banaras (tabla) / Nana Panse or Kudau Singh (pakhawaj), with a bandish

3392.tx: गति (मध्य → द्रुत) · रेले, रौ · व्यंजन पर खत्म होती तेज़ बोलों की अटूट कड़ी; एक-से प्रहार, दम। · निश्चित रचनाएँ (द्रुत) · गत, तुकड़ा, चक्रधार, परन · पहले पढ़ंत, फिर वादन; विविध भंडार ताकि हर कार्यक्रम अलग लगे। · समापन · तिहाई · सम पर ज़ोरदार अंत; फिर श्रोता…

3393.ti: संक्षेप में टिप्पणी: स्वतंत्र वादन का प्रस्तुति क्रम; प्रभावी प्रस्तुतिकरण के गुणतत्त्व; पढ़ंत की आवश्यकता
3393.tx: क्रम सबसे विस्तारशील (पेशकार) से कम विस्तारशील (कायदा, रेला) और फिर निश्चित की ओर, और सबसे ज़्यादा उपज (पेशकार में नए बोल) से कम उपज (कायदे में नए बोल नहीं) की ओर जाता है। ज़्यादातर उपज पहले आधे हिस्से में होती है, जहाँ धीमी लय उसे आसान बनाती है; वादक पहले …

3394.tx: 3) पढ़ंत निश्चित रचनाएँ बजाने से पहले हाथ पर ताली-खाली देते हुए, रचनाकार का नाम आदर से लेकर, बोलकर सुनाई जाती हैं। तेज़ गति में भी साफ़ पढ़ंत प्रस्तुति को आकर्षक बनाती है; इससे याद रहता है, बोलों का वज़न समझ आता है, आत्मविश्वास बढ़ता है और श्रोता रचना समझकर…

3395.ti: संक्षेप में टिप्पणी: स्वतंत्र वादन का प्रस्तुति क्रम; प्रभावी प्रस्तुतिकरण के गुणतत्त्व; पढ़ंत की आवश्यकता
3395.tx: आयोजकों के दिए समय में पूरा करें; विनम्रता और शांत मंच-उपस्थिति। बड़ा रचना-भंडार; लय और लयकारी पर अधिकार; नई तिहाइयाँ और प्रस्तार जो वादक की अपनी सोच दिखाएँ। ताक़त और नज़ाकत का संतुलन: इच्छाशक्ति से ज़ोरदार बजाना और ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा आवाज़ करना एक बात नहीं…

3396.ti: संक्षेप में टिप्पणी: स्वतंत्र वादन का प्रस्तुति क्रम; प्रभावी प्रस्तुतिकरण के गुणतत्त्व; पढ़ंत की आवश्यकता
3396.tx: वाद्य के सुर और श्रोताओं के मूड पर ध्यान; लहरा ताल और उसके विभागों के अनुकूल हो। 5) पखावज एकल

3397.ti: संक्षेप में टिप्पणी: स्वतंत्र वादन का प्रस्तुति क्रम; प्रभावी प्रस्तुतिकरण के गुणतत्त्व; पढ़ंत की आवश्यकता
3397.tx: पखावज एकल भी इन्हीं सिद्धांतों पर अपनी रचनाओं के साथ चलता है: ठेके के बाद तेज़ बोलों के रेले, फिर निश्चित परनें (गत परन, स्तुति परन, आदेशी/फ़रमाइशी परन) और चक्रदार परनें, पूरी हथेली से खुले, ज़ोरदार बोलों में, अंत में सम पर चक्रदार या तिहाई। ⚑ सही क्रम गुरु…

3398.tx: निष्कर्ष: अच्छा एकल सर्वांगीण होता है: नमन से शुरू, विलंबित से द्रुत और विस्तारशील से निश्चित रचनाओं की ओर, साफ़ पढ़ंत, ताक़त और नज़ाकत का संतुलन, और समय पर सम पर ज़ोरदार तिहाई से अंत। पढ़ंत की आवश्यकता (और) स्मृति: पढ़ंत से ताल और रचनाएँ याद रहती हैं और सह…

3399.tx: बोलों का वज़न: रचना को वैसे ही बोलने से जैसे बजेगी, उसके छिपे वज़न खुलते हैं और कहने का ढंग दिखता है; यह हाथों में उतरता है। कथक: नर्तक परनें बोलता है और तबला या पखावज उन्हें वैसे ही बजाता है, इसलिए पढ़ंत नर्तक और संगतकार को जोड़ती है।

3400.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3400.tx: Give information about any one vocal form of semi-classical music and explain the principles of tabla accompaniment with it. (translated; the paper is in Hindi only)

3401.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3401.tx: Chosen form: Thumri. 1) Thumri: the vocal form Category: semi-classical (upshastriya) singing, along with dadra, tappa, kajri, chaiti and hori. Here the accompanist has more individual freedom than in khayal.

3402.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3402.tx: Nature: thumri is sung in ragas of a light, 'fickle' (chanchal) nature and expresses shringar and other rasas; its beauty lies in expression rather than strict raga elaboration. Parts: it has two portions, the asthayi and the antara; after these the singer …

3403.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3403.tx: Taals: because the ragas are fickle, the taals are too: Deepchandi (the main taal), Addha, Keherwa and Teentaal. 2) Principles of tabla accompaniment with thumri Begin simply: start with a simple, clear Deepchandi theka; tune the tabla exactly to the singer…

3404.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3404.tx: Follow the singer: keep the laya steady and the taali-khaali clear; never disturb the singer's line of thought or the mood of the words.

3405.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3405.tx: Change with the laya: when the singer doubles the laya after the asthayi and antara, Deepchandi turns into Keherwa; its playful nature suits laggis, played in single, double and quadruple layas.

3406.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3406.tx: Laggi-ladi: laggis and ladis are essential when the laya rises; they add to the beauty of the thumri and end with a small tihai or tod back to the theka. Rasa and naad: be sensitive to soft and hard sounds; match the rasa of the thumri; play only with the s…

3407.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3407.tx: Example of a master: Ut. Nizamuddin Khan was a great thumri accompanist, famous for his laggis. Stage of thumri · Taal and laya · What the tabla plays · Asthayi, antara · Deepchandi, madhya · Simple, clear theka · Laya doubled · Keherwa · Laggi-ladi in sing…

3408.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3408.tx: Return · Keherwa → Deepchandi · Small tihai or tod back to the theka · Example from your notes: a bhajan tod-tihai (Accompaniment notes) and laggi phraseTod-tihai often used in light accompaniment: धिंऽऽतके धिंऽतके धिंऽतके. Laggi phrase: धा धिं ना ड़ा. Writ…

3409.ti: One semi-classical vocal form and the principles of tabla accompaniment with it
3409.tx: Conclusion: In thumri the tabla begins with a simple Deepchandi theka, follows the singer's mood, changes to Keherwa with laggi-ladi when the laya doubles, and returns with a small tihai; the accompanist has more freedom here than in khayal, but the singer …

3410.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3410.tx: उप-शास्त्रीय संगीत के अंतर्गत आनेवाली कोई भी एक गायनशैली की जानकारी देकर उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांतों को स्पष्ट कीजिये।

3411.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3411.tx: चुनी गई शैली: ठुमरी। 1) ठुमरी: गायन शैली श्रेणी: उपशास्त्रीय गायन, दादरा, टप्पा, कजरी, चैती और होरी के साथ। यहाँ संगतकार को ख़याल से ज़्यादा व्यक्तिगत छूट होती है। स्वभाव: ठुमरी हल्के, 'चंचल' स्वभाव वाले रागों में गाई जाती है और शृंगार व दूसरे रस व्यक्त करत…

3412.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3412.tx: भाग: इसके दो हिस्से हैं, स्थायी और अंतरा; इनके बाद गायक लय दुगुनी करता है। ताल: राग चंचल हैं, इसलिए ताल भी: दीपचंदी (मुख्य ताल), अद्धा, कहरवा और तीनताल। 2) ठुमरी के साथ तबला संगति के सिद्धांत सरल शुरुआत: सरल, साफ़ दीपचंदी ठेके से शुरू करें; तबला गायक के सा …

3413.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3413.tx: गायक का अनुसरण: लय स्थिर और ताली-खाली साफ़ रखें; गायक के विचार-प्रवाह या शब्दों के भाव में कभी बाधा न डालें। लय के साथ बदलाव: स्थायी और अंतरे के बाद गायक लय दुगुनी करे, तो दीपचंदी कहरवा में बदलती है; उसका चंचल स्वभाव लग्गियों के लायक है, जो एकगुन, दुगुन और …

3414.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3414.tx: लग्गी-लड़ी: लय बढ़ने पर लग्गी और लड़ी ज़रूरी हैं; ये ठुमरी की सुंदरता बढ़ाती हैं और छोटी तिहाई या तोड़ से ठेके पर लौटती हैं। रस और नाद: कोमल और कठोर आवाज़ की समझ रखें; ठुमरी के रस से मेल रखें; गायक के इशारे पर ही बजाएँ और टुकड़े छोटे रखें।

3415.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3415.tx: उस्ताद का उदाहरण: उ. निज़ामुद्दीन खाँ महान ठुमरी संगतकार थे, अपनी लग्गियों के लिए प्रसिद्ध। ठुमरी का चरण · ताल और लय · तबला क्या बजाता है · स्थायी, अंतरा · दीपचंदी, मध्य · सरल, साफ़ ठेका · लय दुगुनी · कहरवा · एकगुन, दुगुन, चौगुन में लग्गी-लड़ी · वापसी · कहर…

3416.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3416.tx: आपके नोट्स से उदाहरण: भजन का तोड़-तिहाई (संगत नोट्स) और लग्गी का वाक्यसुगम संगत में अक्सर बजने वाला तोड़-तिहाई: धिंऽऽतके धिंऽतके धिंऽतके। लग्गी का वाक्य: धा धिं ना ड़ा। पूरी कहरवा लग्गी गुरुजी से लिखें।

3417.ti: एक उपशास्त्रीय गायनशैली और उसके साथ तबले की संगति के सिद्धांत
3417.tx: निष्कर्ष: ठुमरी में तबला सरल दीपचंदी ठेके से शुरू होता है, गायक के भाव का अनुसरण करता है, लय दुगुनी होने पर लग्गी-लड़ी के साथ कहरवा में जाता है, और छोटी तिहाई से लौटता है; यहाँ संगतकार को ख़याल से ज़्यादा छूट है, पर नेतृत्व हमेशा गायक का।

3419.tx: All four are given from your notes (Biographies). Only one is needed for 15 marks, so choose the one with the most detail: Pt. Govindrao Burhanpurkar. Write introduction, training, career, style, books, honours and contribution, and end with a conclusion. 4…

3420.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3420.tx: Birth and place: resident of Burhanpur (Nimad, Madhya Pradesh), hence 'Burhanpurkar'. Training: pakhawaj from Shri Sakharamji, a disciple of Pt. Nanasaheb Panse; dhrupad-dhamar singing from Shri Harihar Bua Kopargaonkar; tabla from Pt. Vamanrao of Hyderabad.

3421.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3421.tx: Career: came into contact with Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar and toured India and abroad (Burma, Ceylon) presenting pakhawaj and tabla; HMV recorded his playing during dancer Uday Shankar's performance. Books: Mridang aur Tabla Vadan Subodh and Bharatiya Taa…

3422.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3422.tx: Honours: 'Mridangacharya' (1929), award of the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, felicitation by President Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Death: 20 June 1957. 1) Ut. Wajid Hussain (Lucknow gharana) Birth and family: born 1906 in Lucknow; son of Ut. Bade Munne Khan; son-in-law…

3423.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3423.tx: Training: from his father from the age of 8, and from khalifa Ut. Abid Hussain Khan.

3424.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3424.tx: Style: very attractive performance with balance between tabla and bayan; ended with gat, paran, rela, tihai and chakradhar; his compositions were usually straight in structure. His gat, gat-paran and rela created a 'rav' (flow), a unique mark of his playing…

3425.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3425.tx: Position and students: khalifa of the Lucknow gharana; taught his son Ut. Afaq Hussain Khan. 2) Ut. Chudiyawale Imam Bakhsh (Farrukhabad gharana)

3426.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3426.tx: Introduction: a famous exponent of the Farrukhabad gharana; his birth and death dates are not recorded. Between about 1850 and 1875 he often accompanied the famous Gwalior singers Ut. Hassu Khan and Ut. Haddu Khan.

3427.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3427.tx: Training: he first played pakhawaj. He then served Ut. Haji Vilayat Ali Khan for several years as his hukka attendant, picked up many tabla skills, and was generously accepted as his disciple. He also learnt a great deal from Haji Saheb's wife, Moti Bibi, w…

3428.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3428.tx: Why 'Chudiyawale': at his ganda-bandhan ceremony Moti Bibi tied a bangle (chudi) on his wrist instead of the usual thread; hence the name. Contribution: composed and popularised many tabla compositions that are still played; one of the senior disciples who …

3429.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3429.tx: Family: his son was Ut. Haider Bakhsh. 3) Pt. Parvat Singh (pakhawaj, Gwalior) Introduction: born in 1879 in Gwalior; grandfather Jorawar Singh and father Sukhdev Singh were senior artists of the Gwalior court; died on 18 July 1951.

3430.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3430.tx: Career: spent his childhood preserving and enriching pakhawaj; lived 15 years in Mumbai accompanying many artists; returned to Gwalior after his father's death and in 1917 became the pakhawaj player of the Gwalior palace.

3431.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3431.tx: Style and honours: commendable command over laya and taal; honoured as 'Vidyakala Visharad' in 1926 by the Darbhanga Naresh (president of Bharat Dharma Mandal). His son Madhav Singh was also supported by the Gwalior court. Pt. Burhanpurkar's place in the tr…

3432.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3432.tx: Nana Panse lineage: his pakhawaj guru Shri Sakharamji was a disciple of Pt. Nanasaheb Panse, so he carried the Nana Panse style: simple, clear technique, smaller parans built on mathematical formulas, 3-3 matra divisions, and a softer, more poetic manner th…

3433.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3433.tx: A complete musician: he learnt dhrupad-dhamar singing as well, so he understood the songs he accompanied; he played both pakhawaj and tabla.

3434.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3434.tx: Gandharva Mahavidyalaya: through Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar he became part of the movement that took music to ordinary people, performed in India, Burma and Ceylon, and was honoured by the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya.

3435.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3435.tx: Teaching through books: Mridang aur Tabla Vadan Subodh and Bharatiya Taal Manjari put pakhawaj and tabla knowledge on paper for students, which is why they are still asked about in exams.

3436.ti: Life and musical contribution of any one artist
3436.tx: Conclusion: Pt. Govindrao Burhanpurkar served music as a performer of both pakhawaj and tabla, as an author of textbooks used by students, and as a link between the Nana Panse tradition and the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya movement of Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

3443.tx: शैली: बहुत आकर्षक वादन, दाएँ-बाएँ का संतुलन; अंत में गत, परन, रेला, तिहाई और चक्रधार; उनकी रचनाएँ आमतौर पर सीधी बनावट की। उनके गत, गत-परन और रेले में एक 'रव' (बहाव) बनता था, जो उनके वादन की अनोखी पहचान थी। 76 की उम्र में भी उनकी रिकॉर्डिंग में तैयारी और दाए…

3449.tx: नाना पानसे परंपरा: उनके पखावज गुरु श्री सखारामजी पं. नानासाहेब पानसे के शिष्य थे, इसलिए वे नाना पानसे शैली के वाहक थे: सरल, साफ़ तकनीक, गणितीय सूत्रों पर छोटी परनें, 3-3 मात्रा के खंड, और कुदौ सिंह बाज से ज़्यादा कोमल, काव्यमय ढंग।
